threatModel.summary: Real Fabric is a ten-minute conference-stage demo in which a React/Vite browser creates or joins an open room through a Cloudflare Worker, receives a participant rejoin credential and a provisioned relay credential, opens an authenticated control-plane WebSocket to a per-room SQLite Durable Object, and publishes or subscribes to independent audio tracks through MoqTransportAdapter and a Cloudflare WebTransport/MOQT relay. There is no live AI pipeline; AI behaviour is labelled presenter simulation. Production and declared staging select MOQT draft 16, cooperative routing, unknown discovery and an unverified transport claim (wrangler.jsonc:3-30,37-48; src/client/session/RoomSession.ts:241-320; src/worker/index.ts:77-143).
assets: Raw microphone audio, Opus frames and decoded PCM, kept in browser memory/worklets and not persisted by application source (src/client/audio/CaptureController.ts:34-43,62-115,147-170; public/audio/mixer-worklet.js:23-67).

The provisioned MOQ_RELAY_TOKEN and its coarse relay publish/subscribe authority, returned to every creator or joiner and appended to the WebTransport URL path (src/worker/env.ts:16-25; src/worker/index.ts:98-143,289-304; src/client/transport/MoqTransportAdapter.ts:225-271,532-540).
Participant identity and control authority: room code, participant ID, rejoin token/hash, role, state and routing ownership (src/client/api.ts:10-17,200-230; src/worker/room.ts:45-68,148-180).
Room-state integrity for membership, routing, AI pipeline/floor, simulation, AI-to-AI turns, expiry and reconnect deadlines (src/worker/room.ts:70-84,535-594,820-855).
Privacy of display names and routing relationships in a complete RoomSnapshot readable by a room-code holder (src/shared/contracts.ts:51-78,126-138; src/worker/index.ts:117-143).

Relay-visible track namespace integrity: demo/<room-code>/<participant-id>/audio/<participant-id>, not independently bound to a participant by the shared credential (src/shared/tracks.ts:17-40; src/client/session/RoomSession.ts:544-580).

Availability controls: creation throttling, room expiry, AI turn cap and bounded simulation counts; concurrent-room, credential-issuance and AI-cost ceilings are absent (src/shared/contracts.ts:24-35; src/worker/room.ts:114-138,383-430; PRODUCT_SPEC_v1-demo_1.md:17-31).
Sanitised telemetry, application logs and privileged Cloudflare build/deployment authority (src/client/telemetry/SessionTelemetry.ts:15-81; src/worker/index.ts:33-73,382-389; package.json:8-18).
trustBoundaries: Unauthenticated Internet caller to Worker API: health and creation are public; joining is open with a room code; full snapshots are readable with the room code; field validation follows whole-body parsing (src/worker/index.ts:77-143; src/worker/validation.ts:11-105).

Participant browser to Durable Object: mutations carry participantId and rejoinToken; routing binds its row to the authenticated participant, while AI, floor, AI-to-AI and presenter operations require only any human role (src/worker/room.ts:272-452,785-810).

Participant browser to control WebSocket: the reusable token is placed in a same-origin query string and authenticated before socket acceptance; only ping/pong client messages are accepted (src/client/api.ts:187-198; src/worker/index.ts:263-280; src/worker/room.ts:466-533).

Worker secret to browser and relay: the same optional secret is returned raw at create/join, held in memory and encoded into the relay URL path (src/worker/relayCredential.ts:1-13; src/worker/index.ts:98-143,289-304; src/client/transport/MoqTransportAdapter.ts:532-597).

Relay-originated setup and media objects to moqtail, TrackPlayer, jitter/deduplication buffers, decoder and mixer; dependency internals and relay are outside the inventory (src/client/transport/MoqTransportAdapter.ts:1-18,307-471; src/client/audio/TrackPlayer.ts:72-136).
Developer/CI principal to Cloudflare deployment through pinned Wrangler; account and approval are external (package.json:8-18; wrangler.jsonc:1-16).
attackerCapabilities: An unauthenticated caller can create a limited number of rooms and join any known room code, but lacks another participant token and deployment credentials (src/worker/index.ts:77-143,327-344).
A room-code holder can read the complete RoomSnapshot without joining (src/worker/index.ts:117-143; src/shared/contracts.ts:126-138).

A joined human receives a reusable participant credential and the configured shared relay token; their participant credential authorises all AI, floor, AI-to-AI and presenter operations because the backend checks only human role (src/worker/index.ts:155-260; src/worker/room.ts:187-452).

A shared relay-token holder gains the externally configured coarse authority; source implements no per-room, participant or track grant and labels routing cooperative (src/worker/index.ts:289-304; src/worker/room.ts:916-920).
A malicious participant publisher or compromised relay can supply setup and media objects to the browser receive path (src/client/transport/MoqTransportAdapter.ts:225-471).
securityObjectives: Keep credentials out of share links, snapshots, telemetry and application logs, and issue only short-lived least-privilege relay authority (src/shared/contracts.ts:140-154; src/client/api.ts:187-219; src/client/telemetry/SessionTelemetry.ts:24-81).

Preserve routing ownership and distinguish ordinary participant authority from presenter/global room authority; never claim relay enforcement while credentials are coarse (src/worker/room.ts:267-452,916-920).
Bound request, room, WebSocket and media-object resources without imposing a legitimate participant-count cap (src/shared/contracts.ts:24-35; src/worker/room.ts:114-138,499-525).

Validate identifiers and input; store only token hashes and require matching active participant credentials (src/worker/index.ts:117-123,306-344; src/worker/validation.ts:11-105; src/worker/room.ts:793-810,1035-1045).

Keep microphone audio transient and close capture, worklets, publications, subscriptions and sockets on leave (src/client/audio/CaptureController.ts:147-170; src/client/session/RoomSession.ts:995-1019).
Bind privileged deployment to the intended account, Worker, environment, revision and payload externally (package.json:8-18; wrangler.jsonc:1-16).
assumptions: Offline review is limited to the exact 93-file snapshot at revision a784122aa18c6b7fbee1ae53d34b054a24d71f0b; deployed secrets, relay acceptance and runtime exploitability are unverified.
No SECURITY.md, supplied threat model, user security context or authoritative knowledge base was available.
Docs say the relay token is configured and expires on 2026-09-01, but source proves only an optional secret reference (README.md:85-92; src/worker/env.ts:16-25).
The Product Spec calls the rejoin token single-use, but source reuses it unchanged after reclaim (PRODUCT_SPEC_v1-demo_1.md:195-201; src/worker/room.ts:596-630,793-810).

The Product Spec calls several operations presenter actions and says each human sees only their routing row, while server authorisation is any human and snapshots contain all rows (PRODUCT_SPEC_v1-demo_1.md:226-237,263-273; src/worker/room.ts:383-452,820-855).
moqtail internals, generated dist, relay, Cloudflare platform logging and deployed bindings are outside the authorised inventory.

deferred.reason: Independent baseline candidate awaiting parent source validation.

candidate.rule: A Worker-wide relay bearer credential is disclosed to every room creator and joiner
candidate.attacker: Any unauthenticated Internet user who creates a room, or any person who joins a known room.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Relay credentials must be short-lived and least-privilege, with participant publication and subscription authority enforced.
candidate.source_to_sink: Unauthenticated create and open join handlers include relayCredential(env); that helper returns the same trimmed MOQ_RELAY_TOKEN without room, participant, track, action or expiry scoping; the browser inserts it into the relay WebTransport URL.
candidate.impact: If accepted with the documented coarse authority, a modified client can bypass cooperative routing, subscribe or publish outside UI permissions, impersonate tracks and disrupt participants.
supporting_source_evidence: Creation needs no participant credential yet returns the Worker relay secret.
The same secret is returned for creation and every join.
No source mints participant- or room-specific grants or derives relay permissions from routing.
counterevidence: The token is a Worker secret and omitted from logs, telemetry, snapshots and share links.
Identifiers are opaque and UI labels routing cooperative.
Live relay acceptance and deployed scope are unverified.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Mint short-lived room/participant credentials restricting publication and subscriptions; revoke them on routing, leave and expiry; do not expose a relay-wide secret if enforcement is unavailable.

candidate.rule: Any joined human can execute presenter-only global room controls
candidate.attacker: Any attendee who knows the room code and joins normally.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Global presenter actions must be authorised to a presenter or owner, not any human.
candidate.source_to_sink: All AI, floor, AI-to-AI and presenter mutations call assertHuman, which verifies only human role; the browser presenter flag affects only UI visibility, and requestFloor accepts arbitrary aiId.
candidate.impact: A malicious attendee can add/remove AIs, fabricate pipeline state, reconfigure simulation, enable AI loops or wedge floor ownership.
supporting_source_evidence: Open membership gives every attendee a valid human credential.
No owner or presenter role is persisted or checked.
Every global action accepts any valid human credential.
counterevidence: Anonymous, invalid-token and AI-role callers are rejected.
Participant routing updates enforce ownership.
The client hides presenter controls.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Persist a room owner/presenter principal and require a distinct server capability for global mutations; validate AI targets; limit ordinary humans to participant-owned operations.

candidate.rule: A reusable participant bearer token is placed in the WebSocket URL query string
candidate.attacker: A party able to read handshake URLs from diagnostics, platform/proxy logs, monitoring or support artefacts.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Reusable authentication secrets must not be placed in URLs commonly recorded by infrastructure.
candidate.source_to_sink: roomEventsUrl appends participant ID and reusable rejoin token; Worker and Durable Object authenticate with that query token; reclaim returns it unchanged.
candidate.impact: A disclosed URL permits participant impersonation, event access and authenticated mutations.
supporting_source_evidence: The URL contains the bearer used for HTTP mutations.
No one-time socket ticket exists.
No rotation occurs on reclaim.
counterevidence: WSS protects transit, the token is high entropy and only its hash is persisted.
Application logs omit queries and exports omit the token.
Platform URL logging is external and unverified.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Exchange the main credential for a single-use short-expiry socket ticket and rotate the rejoin credential on reclaim.

candidate.rule: Room joins and control WebSockets have no per-room or per-credential resource limits
candidate.attacker: A malicious room-code holder or participant replaying their credential.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Open membership must not permit one source or credential to allocate unbounded room state and sockets.
candidate.source_to_sink: Only creation is rate-limited; every join inserts participant/routing state and broadcasts. Every valid socket is accepted and the same credential can open many sockets receiving all broadcasts.
candidate.impact: Attackers can create quadratic routing work or broadcast amplification, exhausting Durable Object resources.
supporting_source_evidence: No join velocity or socket-per-credential limit exists.
Participant insertion adds routing work.
A credential is replayable across concurrent sockets.
counterevidence: Room codes are non-guessable.
Rooms expire, creation is limited and Cloudflare has ceilings.
Product forbids a participant-count admission cap.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Rate-limit abusive join velocity without a count cap; bound sockets per participant; add mutation budgets, backpressure and visible degradation.

candidate.rule: Untrusted JSON bodies are fully allocated and parsed before application size and rate controls
candidate.attacker: Any unauthenticated caller of room creation and callers reaching mutation routes.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Untrusted bodies must be bounded before whole-body allocation and cheap admission controls should precede parsing.
candidate.source_to_sink: readJsonObject immediately awaits request.json(); field validation and the creation limiter run only after parsing.
candidate.impact: Oversized or deeply structured bodies can consume Worker CPU/memory before rejection.
supporting_source_evidence: No Content-Length ceiling or bounded reader exists.
Field limits apply after parsing.
The create limiter runs after parsing.
counterevidence: Only JSON is accepted and fields are bounded.
Cloudflare request/isolate limits contain blast radius.
Legitimate bodies are small.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Reject oversized declared bodies, use a bounded reader when absent, apply admission controls before parsing and enforce shallow schemas.

candidate.rule: Inbound media objects have no per-track object-count or byte budget
candidate.attacker: A malicious joined publisher with relay access or a compromised relay.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: The receive pipeline must bound memory, decode and scheduling work for untrusted publishers.
candidate.source_to_sink: Every object reaches TrackPlayer; framing permits 16-bit payload length; deduplication retains unbounded IDs per group; jitter buffering scans, appends, sorts and time-prunes without count or byte ceilings.
candidate.impact: A burst of unique valid objects can freeze or crash subscribed browsers.
supporting_source_evidence: Unique IDs in one group are not count-bounded.
Four retained groups do not cap IDs per group.
A 200 ms rule does not cap a burst.
Per-insert sorting creates superlinear CPU work.
counterevidence: Malformed frames are rejected and one payload is capped at 65,535 bytes.
Old jitter frames, old groups and the mixer ring are bounded.
WebTransport flow control does not establish application budgets.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Enforce encoded-size/cadence limits, per-track object/byte/decode budgets, bounded IDs and frames, a bounded ordered structure and abusive-subscription quarantine.

deferred.reason: Focused investigation candidate awaiting parent source validation.

candidate.rule: Unbounded per-group playback deduplication retains attacker-controlled object identifiers
candidate.attacker: A malicious joined publisher using a modified client and the relay credential on its automatically subscribed human track, or a compromised relay.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Per-track receive state must have explicit object-count and byte bounds.
candidate.source_to_sink: Relay group/object identifiers flow through MoqTransportAdapter and RoomSession to TrackPlayer.accept. PlaybackDeduplicator runs before envelope validation and adds every unique objectId to an unbounded Set. A constant groupId with varying objectId grows for TrackPlayer lifetime; repeated malformed objects do not quarantine the track.
candidate.impact: A sustained same-group stream can grow the victim tab heap until UI/audio failure or tab termination.
supporting_source_evidence: Map<number, Set<number>> adds unbounded object IDs.
A single group never triggers four-group pruning.
Every other real human track is automatically subscribed.
No object-rate, byte-rate, malformed threshold or quarantine exists.
counterevidence: Closing clears the map.
New distinct groups eventually prune older groups.
The session log is bounded.
External flow control is not a retained-entry cap.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Validate before deduplication; add per-track object and byte budgets, per-group identifier caps, progress checks and quarantine.

deferred.reason: Focused investigation candidate awaiting parent source validation.

candidate.rule: Count-unbounded jitter insertion and decoder submission permit algorithmic media-burst denial of service
candidate.attacker: A malicious joined publisher sending valid unique envelopes far above the expected cadence, or a compromised relay.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: The latency target must also impose count, byte and decode-work limits.
candidate.source_to_sink: AdaptiveJitterBuffer scans, appends, sorts and time-filters a count-unbounded array on each valid object. Frames inside the 200 ms arrival window survive. drain submits all eligible frames to AudioDecoder without a work budget or decodeQueueSize check.
candidate.impact: A short burst can cause superlinear main-thread work, retain many copied payloads and flood the decoder, causing audio/UI failure.
supporting_source_evidence: The 200 ms threshold is not a count bound.
Unique sequences with near-identical receive times survive.
One payload can be 65,535 bytes plus header.
No decoder-queue or inbound-rate degradation metric exists.
counterevidence: Older frames are removed.
Mixer ring, cancelled groups, concealment and decoded AudioData lifetime are bounded.
External backpressure is not an application guarantee.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Use a bounded sequence structure; cap objects/bytes; validate cadence and frame size; budget drains; gate decoder queue; quarantine persistent offenders.

candidate.rule: A static relay-wide credential is returned to every participant without room, publisher or subscription scope
candidate.attacker: Any unauthenticated room creator or joined human using a modified MOQT client.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Relay credentials must bind participant, room, own publication and authorised subscriptions.
candidate.source_to_sink: Public create and join return one configured token. The adapter authenticates with it and accepts caller-selected track addresses; track names are deterministic and routing is cooperative.
candidate.impact: A holder can attempt relay namespace publication or subscription outside client routing; actual collision/spoofing depends on external relay semantics.
supporting_source_evidence: One environment secret is used without claim minting.
Creation is public.
Adapter operations are not reconciled to routing.
Routing is cooperative.
counterevidence: Credential is omitted from snapshots and held in memory.
Identifiers are high entropy.
Ordinary client restricts itself.
Relay acceptance, ACLs, expiry and collision semantics are unverified.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Mint short-lived per-room and participant credentials for own publication and server-authorised subscriptions; otherwise keep transport unavailable or add enforcement.

candidate.rule: Worker parses unbounded JSON bodies before rate limiting or participant authentication
candidate.attacker: An unauthenticated creator or a caller targeting room mutation routes.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Public routes must reject bodies larger than their small schema before buffering and parsing.
candidate.source_to_sink: readJsonObject checks only Content-Type then calls request.json. Field validation, creation rate limiting and participant authentication occur later.
candidate.impact: Repeated oversized JSON forces disproportionate Worker CPU and memory before rejection, risking cost and demo disruption.
supporting_source_evidence: No Content-Length check, streaming counter or 413 response exists.
Legitimate fields are tiny.
Creation limiter runs after parse.
counterevidence: Content-Type is checked.
Join checks room existence.
Platform limits make each request finite but do not supply a small app bound.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Enforce a small declared and streamed byte limit before JSON.parse; rate-limit creation first; authenticate mutations before parsing where feasible.

candidate.rule: Unauthenticated room creation discloses a Worker-wide relay publish/subscribe bearer
candidate.attacker: An unauthenticated room creator.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: A Worker relay secret must not become an unscoped end-user bearer.
candidate.source_to_sink: POST /api/rooms returns relayCredential(env); that returns MOQ_RELAY_TOKEN unchanged; the client places it in the WebTransport URL and can call publish, subscribe and subscribeNamespace with caller-selected addresses.
candidate.impact: If the relay accepts the documented authority, any creator can bypass room routing and attempt arbitrary publication or subscription; external cross-room semantics remain unverified.
supporting_source_evidence: No minting, claims, room binding, participant binding or expiry exists.
Worker comments describe publish and subscribe authority.
Adapter accepts arbitrary track and namespace arguments.
counterevidence: Creation is throttled.
Responses are no-store and logs/rendering redact the token.
Relay acceptance, expiry and enforcement are trace-unverified.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Never return the Worker-wide secret; mint short-lived per-room, participant, role and namespace credentials, or keep transport unavailable until enforcement exists.

candidate.rule: Open-room joining independently discloses the same relay-wide bearer without an issuance throttle
candidate.attacker: A holder of a valid room code.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Open joining must not grant relay authority beyond the participant's permitted tracks and issuance must be throttled.

Every join receives the same credential.
Snapshot and deterministic naming expose namespace inputs.
No issuance budget exists.

Credential is absent from public snapshots and logs.
Relay acceptance and undocumented scope are unverified.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Mint a scoped credential after a controlled join; rate-limit issuance per source and room without imposing a participant-count cap.

candidate.attacker: An ordinary joined human with their own credential.

sessionStorage is never verified as authority.

candidate.recommended_remediation: Persist a creator/presenter capability and require it for presenter and AI-to-AI administration; record turn progression from a trusted orchestration path.

candidate.attacker: An ordinary joined human.

candidate.attacker: An ordinary joined human.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Floor holders and queued entries must be active AIs and release must prove control of the turn.

Duplicate queue IDs deduplicate.

candidate.attacker: Any room-code holder.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Each human may see only their own detailed routing row; others receive aggregate context.

Room data is ephemeral.

candidate.rule: A reusable participant bearer is placed in the WebSocket query string instead of a single-use socket ticket
candidate.attacker: A reader of external access, proxy or diagnostic logs that record the handshake URL.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: WebSocket handshakes must use short-lived single-use tickets, not the general reusable credential.
candidate.source_to_sink: roomEventsUrl appends participant ID and rejoin token; Worker and Durable Object read and authenticate it. The same token authorises mutations, reclaim returns it unchanged and it is not consumed.
candidate.impact: If an external system records the URL, a log reader can replay the credential for sockets, identity reclaim, routing and global operations guarded only by assertHuman.
supporting_source_evidence: Full bearer is appended as token=.
No independent token expiry or consumption exists.
Reclaim returns the same token and can act while connected.
counterevidence: Application logs omit query strings.
External full-URL logging is unverified.
Token is random, hashed at rest and bounded by leave/room expiry.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Mint and atomically consume a short-lived socket ticket; never put the rejoin credential in a URL; rotate it after reclaim.

supporting_source_evidence: Participant tags are not used for limits.

Full snapshot size grows with membership/routing.
broadcast iterates all sockets.

Only ping client messages are accepted.
Room expiry closes sockets.
Platform quotas are external.

candidate.rule: Unthrottled open-room joins permit unbounded participant and routing allocation
candidate.attacker: A malicious holder of a valid room code.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Open membership remains uncapped but join and issuance rates and per-request work must be bounded.
candidate.source_to_sink: Every non-reclaim join creates a token, participant, routing row per active AI, broadcast and complete snapshot. The route checks existence with one snapshot before join creates another.
candidate.impact: A room-code holder can rapidly grow participant and human-by-AI routing state, snapshot size, broadcasts and credential responses.
supporting_source_evidence: Only room creation is rate-limited.
Membership tests explicitly reject a count cap.
Each human seeds routing for every AI.
Join returns a full snapshot and relay credential.
counterevidence: Room code is high entropy.
Inputs are bounded.
Rooms hard-stop at twenty minutes.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Use per-source and per-room token-bucket join/issuance limits with burst capacity, avoid double snapshot serialisation and budget routing work without a participant-count cap.

candidate.rule: Arbitrary room-code probes force persistent SQLite Durable Object initialisation outside the creation limiter
candidate.attacker: An unauthenticated remote caller.
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Only rate-limited room creation should allocate persistent room objects; unknown lookups must stay cheap and read-only.
candidate.source_to_sink: Any syntactically valid 20-character code maps through getByName to a Room. The constructor runs migrate, creating SQLite tables and schema_meta before getSnapshot returns null. No room metadata or alarm cleans the uninitialised object.
candidate.impact: Attackers can generate unlimited codes and create persistent SQLite-backed object schemas outside the creation limiter, causing storage, billing or availability pressure.
supporting_source_evidence: Path accepts arbitrary 20-character codes.
getByName deterministically maps them.
Constructor always migrates and writes schema metadata.
No alarm exists without room_meta.
counterevidence: Lookup returns 404 and creates no room_meta/participants/credentials.
Exact Cloudflare billing effect is external.
Each schema is small.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Check existence in a rate-limited registry or validate signed room codes before getByName; make uninitialised lookup non-writing; expire abandoned allocations.
